{{nihongo|'''Yuge Shrine'''|弓削神社 (高島市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Yuge Shrine''' (ゆげじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in Imazu Town, {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|Q845794|qid=Q845794}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is considered to correspond to the “Yuge Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} under {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}} {{ill|Takashima District, Shiga|Q11669692|qid=Q11669692|lt=Takashima District}}, and is regarded as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. However, it lies outside a fence installed to prevent damage by wild animals, making it difficult to visit under normal circumstances.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}
* {{ill|Prince Yuge|Q3076827|qid=Q3076827}}
The {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}} suggests that the deity may be {{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}, the ancestor of Yuge no Sukune.

=== Shrine crest ===
* Left-facing triple tomoe

=== History ===
The date of establishment is unknown, but it is said that when Emperor Ōjin was on his way to {{ill|Tsuruga, Fukui|Q847581|qid=Q847581|lt=Tsuruga}}, he rested at this place, and the pillow stone used at that time was enshrined as the sacred object. In the 4th year of {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}}, the Hachiman deity was enshrined together. In the 9th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, it was ranked as a village shrine.

=== Festivals ===
* Annual festival: November 3
